claims.text: Dopamine agonists (cabergoline, bromocriptine): less effective than somatostatin analogs;
claims.quote: Dopamine receptor agonists (cabergoline, bromocriptine): These act on dopamine 2 receptors (D2R) in the pituitary gland and are less effective than somatostatin analogs.
They are often used as adjuncts.

claims.text: Cabergoline is more potent than bromocriptine at lowering GH.
claims.quote: Cabergoline is more potent than bromocriptine in lowering GH levels.

claims.text: Bromocriptine has been used in pregnant women w acromegaly without fetal harm.
claims.quote: Bromocriptine has been used in pregnant women with acromegaly to manage the signs and symptoms without causing adverse fetal harm.
